correctness.rationale: For each inverse row of the finite nilpotent Neumann expansion, triangular support makes the new diagonal unit coordinate orthogonal to earlier inverse rows. The off-diagonal residual row norm is at most the row budget times the largest preceding row norm; induction bounds its squared defect by a finite geometric sum. Summation yields the sharp finite Frobenius maximum, attained term by term on a weighted bidiagonal chain. A universal Euclidean upper bound follows from the Frobenius defect, while the explicit chain with many leaves attains the matching square-root dimension coefficient. Supplementary exact-rational and numerical finite cases were run from checker.py; all passed. Infinite-size conclusions rely on the analytical proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The recently proposed DIAG_DOM coarse/fine splitting method explicitly controls absolute off-diagonal row sums of a triangular fine block. The theorem identifies an exact finite Frobenius bound and the sharp dimension-normalized Euclidean inverse amplification under precisely that user-selected budget, showing that dimension-independent row control need not yield uniform Euclidean solve sensitivity. The structural difference between a chain and a chain-with-leaves explains where apparent pathwise stability fails under wide branching and provides a quantitative benchmark for sparse triangular solves.
